summary: The Mamaroneck River is a freshwater stream in Southern Westchester County, New York. It forms in White Plains and Harrison, flows south through the Town and Village of Mamaroneck, and empties into Mamaroneck Harbor and Long Island Sound. The note also explains the river's name, which comes from a local Native American word.
one_line: The Mamaroneck River is a freshwater stream in Southern Westchester County, New York, flowing from White Plains and Harrison into Long Island Sound.
key_facts: The Mamaroneck River is a freshwater stream located in Southern Westchester County, New York.
The Mamaroneck River forms in White Plains and Harrison.
The Mamaroneck River flows south through Mamaroneck Town and Village.
The Mamaroneck River empties into Mamaroneck Harbor and Long Island Sound.
The name of the Mamaroneck River comes from a local Native American word meaning "where the fresh water meets the salt water."
The Mamaroneck River flows into Long Island Sound.
